areas.title: Pipeline and services (Python)
areas.what: The steps of a search, the web server, and the processes the cluster is made of.

files.does: A gate in front of slow work: at most `concurrency` jobs run at once, the rest wait, and a waiting job LEAVES the queue the moment its deadline passes.
Bring your own model: understand the request with the visitor's own API key instead of the local model.
One search over several catalogues: a general one and specialists.
Checks on the search candidates before an outfit is built, each one reported in plain words (nothing is changed silently).
Claude API client with a HARD spend cap, for small paid checks only. The key comes from .env (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), never printed or logged.
Dominant garment colour from a product photo, and a small colour-harmony rule set.
Selecting an apparel sample from Marqo-GS-10M (a mixed-category Google Shopping ranking dataset).
Duplicate products: the same photo or the same item listed again under another seller's title.
Text and image embeddings through open_clip (weights only: no remote code is executed).
Encoder service: turns request text into the numbers the shards search with (Marqo-FashionSigLIP, the only process holding the model).
Personalisation by feedback (the Rocchio method): move the query toward products the shopper liked and away from ones they did not.
A small knowledge graph: occasion -> usage -> (gender, usage) -> garment types, by outfit role.
Content-safety guard for shopper requests. Runs BEFORE the language model and the search.
A small persistent vector index: product ids + unit-length embeddings + the facts needed to trust it later.
Ingest worker: takes new-product messages from the job queue, embeds the photo, adds the product to EVERY replica of its shard.
A small durable job queue with Amazon SQS semantics, backed by SQLite (survives restarts).
Ranking metrics. Relevance comes from the dataset: each ranked product has a graded score (1-100, higher = better).
Choose one product per piece so the outfit goes together, not just each piece in isolation.
Recorded runs for the public Viewer: real pipeline traces made safe to publish.
One JSON log line per request, carrying the search's ticket number (the x-request-id header the router sends).
What running Lucida takes from THIS computer, measured now: memory of the web server, of the local model server (Ollama) and of any local
Retrieval baselines and brute-force cosine search.
Web backend for the UI: one request runs the whole pipeline, and every step is streamed to the page as a small "trace" event.
One shard worker: holds a slice of the products and answers "your best matches for this vector".
Sharded search: split all catalogues' products over N shards by product id, scatter every query to all shards, gather and merge.
The same queue calls as genkart.jobqueue.JobQueue, on Amazon SQS (FIFO queue + its dead-letter queue). IngestWorker works with either.
The consented study: does a drawn preview change how people rate the SAME search results?
What the consented study found: the same search results rated with and without the AI drawing beside them.
Where the consented study keeps its answers. Two places, one small interface (save / has / delete a document by id, delete_many in one request):
Turn a shopper's free-text request into a structured product search plan with a local language model (LangChain + Ollama).

areas.title: Router (TypeScript)
areas.what: Asks all shards at once, merges the answers, survives failures.

files.does: Router settings read from the environment: ports, shard addresses (with replicas), deadlines, hedge delay, in-flight limit.

The router: asks the encoder, asks every shard at once (failover and hedging across replicas), merges, refuses past the limit with HTTP 429.

areas.title: Tests
areas.what: What is checked on every change.

files.does: The encoder's gate: at most N jobs at once, and a waiting job whose deadline passed is dropped, never run.
Rater agreement: lifted kappa functions, prompt-level bootstrap, and the analyze_agreement script on synthetic ratings.
Bring your own model: the visitor's key is validated, used for one request, and must never appear in an event, an error, a repr or a response.
Searching several catalogues: general first, specialists when the match is weak, gender respected.
The candidate checks: slot fit, no children's items unless asked, one gender per outfit, the named colour first, and never an empty slot.
The Claude spend caps: per purpose, and one total over every purpose that no script can pass.
The Cloud Run service must keep the live name genkart-lab (a new name is a new service with a new URL, which breaks the Pages site's PHOTO_BASE).
Reading a garment's colour from its photo, and the colour-harmony score of an outfit.
The rule that decides which dataset queries are about clothing.
Finding near-identical products across catalogues and keeping one of each.
The hosted image's settings: every ENV line is a clean list of NAME=value words, and the settings the hosted Lab depends on are all there.
The documentation must cover the project: every code file is on the map with a description, every logged run is cited by the site
The encoder reads only real files inside data/: ../ tricks, symlinks that point outside, folders and missing files are all refused.
The feedback step: a query moves toward liked products, away from disliked ones, stays unit length, and is unchanged with no feedback.
The knowledge graph: occasion words, garment suggestions, replacing generic pieces, adding missing roles.
The safety guard: ordinary fashion allowed, harmful and injection requests refused.
The vector index: best first, exact match found, save and load, damaged files detected.
Adding products through the queue: every replica gets it, retries do not duplicate, a bad photo is parked.
The local queue: hiding time, acknowledge, dead-letter after too many tries, repeated keys ignored.
scripts/make_report.py: offline, deterministic, fully filled, and its numbers equal the values in the run files.
The ranking measures (DCG, NDCG, recall, reciprocal rank) against hand calculations.
Nothing that identifies the owner's cloud account may sit in a file git would publish: no bucket name, instance id, public address or key.
Building an outfit: harmony swaps, keeping the best match when alternatives are much worse, no repeated product.
scripts/make_pilot_ratings_set.py: whitelist of keys, string ids, deterministic, counts equal the source files.
ratings_from_paste: tolerant of messy pasted text, strict about ids, words and conflicting duplicates.
Recorded runs must never carry a photo address, and must not republish ids or titles from catalogues the project rules keep local.
One JSON log line per request with its ticket number; hostile ticket numbers cannot forge log lines.
The memory numbers come from the operating system and Ollama's own report: a snapshot must be well formed even with nothing running.
The pipeline streams one event per step, in order, with exact product ids as text. Everything outside is replaced by fakes: no model,
The web server's call to the router: HTTP 429 means "busy, ask again shortly", not "the search failed".
Splitting products over shards gives exactly the single-process answer for any shard count.
SqsJobQueue and the S3 photo hook, against a small fake of the SQS calls we use (no AWS needed).
The consented study's server side: off unless configured, input checked, one answer per participant and prompt, withdrawal deletes, a failing store says 503.
The study's analysis: per-participant with-minus-without differences, only people with both arms, honest when there is no data.
The study's answer storage: the local file store (replace, delete, survive a damaged line) and the Firestore store's requests, checked against a fake Google.
Checking the language model's plan against the sentence: invented colours and genders are removed.
